name: Lake Baikal
scope: A crescent rift lake in southern Siberia, the deepest and oldest lake on Earth. T1: Baikal holds about a FIFTH (~20%) of all the unfrozen fresh water on the planet -- more than all five North American Great Lakes combined (the vast water is the hook; answer = 'the most fresh water of any single lake'). T2: at 25+ million years it is the world's OLDEST lake (invert the wonder: the age/size is the hook, 'oldest lake' the answer). T3: its floor plunges past 1,642 m, making it the DEEPEST lake on Earth. T4: the nerpa is the world's only exclusively FRESHWATER seal, living 1,700+ km from any sea -- the place-fact is that Baikal is the ONLY lake with its own resident seal. T5 (winter ice): in a hard freeze the ultra-clear ice cracks into turquoise shards and trapped methane freezes into stacked white 'frozen bubble' discs. Further rungs: over 300 rivers pour IN but only ONE -- the Angara -- flows OUT; Baikal sits in a RIFT where Eurasia is slowly pulling apart (the basin widens ~2 cm/yr and may one day become an ocean -- teach 'rift lake'); the water is transparent to ~40 m; unusually for so deep a lake it is OXYGENATED to its full depth, so life lives more than a kilometre down; 'Shaman Rock' at Olkhon Island is sacred in Buryat shamanism (culture/place).
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Baikal, attempted first -- HTTP 403 to harness fetcher); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Baikal, Britannica 'Lake Baikal', and the task exemplar. Figures cross-checked: 1,642 m depth, 25-30 Myr age, ~20-23% of world unfrozen surface fresh water, Pusa sibirica (nerpa) sole freshwater seal, Angara sole outflow.
framing_note: Every rung's answer is a concrete fact about THIS lake; a distractor set of OTHER real superlatives (largest by area = Superior/Caspian, saltiest = Dead Sea, longest = Tanganyika) keeps all four live. Lead with the scene, never 'What is the oldest lake?'. Teach 'rift lake' before testing it. The nerpa rung is the dinner-test payoff. LANE: the nerpa seal is an ANIMAL -- keep the answer the PLACE-fact (the only lake with its own freshwater seal; oxygenated to full depth), never the seal's biology (that belongs to the animal bank).

name: The Dead Sea
scope: A hypersaline lake at the bottom of the Jordan Rift, on the Israel-Jordan-West Bank frontier. T1: its shore sits about 430-440 m BELOW sea level (and dropping) -- the LOWEST dry land on Earth (the number is the hook; answer = 'lowest land on Earth'). T2: at ~34% salt (about ten times the ocean) the brine is so dense you FLOAT without trying -- you can lie back and read a newspaper on the surface (answer = you cannot sink / you float). T3: it is ENDORHEIC -- the Jordan River is the only major inflow and NOTHING flows out; water leaves only by evaporation (teach 'endorheic'). T3: nothing lives in the brine -- no fish, no plants -- which is why ancient writers named it the 'Dead' Sea. T4: the lake is SHRINKING roughly a metre a year as the Jordan is diverted upstream. T5: as the water drops, fresh groundwater dissolves buried salt and the old shoreline collapses into thousands of SINKHOLES (>6,000 recorded) that open without warning (dinner-test payoff). Further rungs: it lies in the Jordan Rift / Dead Sea Transform, a crack where two plates slide past each other (why it is so low); Mount Sodom nearby is a mountain of salt (halite) and the biblical 'pillar of salt' is legend (label it); the lake is mined for potash, and its black mineral mud has been a cosmetic since antiquity.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Dead_Sea, attempted first -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea, Britannica 'Dead Sea', CNN 2025 sinkhole reporting, deadsea.com water-level tracker. Figures: ~439.8 m below sea level (mid-2020s), ~34.2% salinity (~9.6x ocean), decline >1 m/yr since 2001, >6,000 sinkholes on the western shore.
framing_note: Distractors = other salty/low/endorheic places (the Caspian, Great Salt Lake, Lake Assal, the Aral). Accuracy rail: state the level as a RANGE (~430-440 m below sea level and DROPPING), never a frozen number; 'so salty you float' is brine DENSITY, not magic; the Lot's-wife salt pillar is LEGEND, flag it. Teach 'endorheic'. Dinner-test = the shore collapsing into sinkholes / floating-and-reading. LANE: the Dead Sea Scrolls / Qumran are a HISTORY episode -- do NOT build a scrolls-content rung here.
history_overlap: History bank owns the Dead Sea Scrolls / Qumran episode -- keep geography rungs to the lake's landscape, salinity, shrinking and sinkholes; a scrolls-content rung would duplicate history.

name: The Caspian Sea
scope: A vast landlocked body between Europe and Asia, ringed by five countries. T2: at 371,000 km2 it is the LARGEST lake on Earth -- bigger than Germany -- so huge that ancient and modern people alike call it a 'Sea' (size is the hook; answer = 'the world's largest lake'). T3: it is ENDORHEIC -- the Volga and other rivers pour IN, but no river flows OUT to any ocean; it balances only inflow against evaporation (teach 'endorheic'). T4: its water is BRACKISH, about a THIRD as salty as the ocean -- the leftover of an ancient sea (the Paratethys) that was cut off from the world ocean millions of years ago, which is why a 'lake' tastes of the sea. T4: because it is a closed basin, its level RISES and FALLS by metres over decades, marching Baku's shoreline in and out. T5: on the Absheron Peninsula, natural gas seeps burn as eternal FLAMES on the ground (Yanar Dag) and once fuelled the Zoroastrian fire temple of Ateshgah -- earning the shore the name 'Land of Fire' (dinner-test payoff). Further rung: the Kara-Bogaz-Gol, a scorching shallow gulf so evaporative it siphons Caspian water in and lays down vast salt/mirabilite flats.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Caspian_Sea, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspian_Sea, worldatlas.com Caspian/endorheic-lakes, New World Encyclopedia. Figures: 371,000 km2 (largest lake by area & volume), ~1.2% salinity (~1/3 ocean), Paratethys remnant, five bordering states.
framing_note: The 'sea that is really a lake' puzzle is the spine: teach 'endorheic' and the Paratethys cut-off. Distractors = other big inland waters (Superior, Baikal, the Aral, the Black Sea). Accuracy rail: it is BRACKISH (~1.2%, a third of ocean), not fresh and not sea-salty. Dinner-test = Yanar Dag's eternal flames / 'largest lake called a sea'. LANE: Caspian CAVIAR is a FOOD (cooking bank) and its sturgeon is ANIMAL -- do NOT build a caviar/sturgeon rung; keep answers to the basin, its origin, its shifting level, and the burning gas seeps. Baku OIL as industry is economics -- frame the flames as a NATURAL wonder + sacred site, not petroleum.

name: The Aral Sea
scope: A former inland sea between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, most of it now the Aralkum Desert. T2: within living memory the Aral was the world's FOURTH-largest lake; today most of it is a salt-and-sand DESERT -- the Aralkum, the newest desert on Earth (it vanished; answer = 'it dried up / became a desert'). T3: it died because SOVIET planners diverted its two feeder rivers -- the Amu Darya and Syr Darya -- to irrigate COTTON ('white gold') across the desert; starved of inflow, the sea evaporated away (the cause rung -- active voice, a named agent). T3: at the old port of MOYNAQ, rusting fishing trawlers now sit on dry sand more than 100 km from any water -- a 'ship graveyard' (dinner-test payoff). T4: the bare lakebed is laced with salt, pesticide and fertilizer, and the wind lifts TOXIC DUST STORMS that carry across Central Asia and settle on distant glaciers. T5: Kazakhstan fought back -- the KOKARAL DAM (2005) walled off the small NORTH Aral, and behind it the water and the fish have partly RETURNED (the recovery is real). Further rung: as the water fell, the seabed revealed a medieval settlement and mausoleum (Kerderi) -- proof the lake has grown and shrunk before.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Aral_Sea, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aral_Sea, NPR 'Aral Sea shrinking' interactive, Global Voices 2026 'North Aral' report. Figures: former 4th-largest lake, >90% surface lost, Kokaral Dam completed 2005, North Aral level +12 m by 2008, Moynaq now 30-100 km from shore.
framing_note: This is the config's honest-environmental-record topic (moral_vision sec 3.1) -- so the cause rung names the agent in ACTIVE VOICE (Soviet planners diverted the rivers for cotton), never 'the rivers were diverted'; and the North-Aral recovery is stated honestly so it is not one-sided doom. NOT climate-apocalypse polemic -- a specific, human-caused, place-written disaster. Distractors = other shrinking/vanished lakes (Lake Chad, the Salton Sea, Owens Lake, the Dead Sea). Dinner-test = the ship graveyard at Moynaq. Marked vision_mandated so the moral audit checks the attribution and the both-directions honesty.

name: Lake Titicaca
scope: A high lake in the Andes on the Peru-Bolivia border, cradled in the Altiplano basin. T1: at 3,812 m (about 12,500 ft) up in the mountains, Titicaca is the world's HIGHEST navigable lake -- full-size boats sail a lake as high as some peaks (the altitude is the hook; answer = 'highest navigable lake'). T2: the UROS people live on floating ISLANDS they weave entirely from totora reeds -- when the reeds rot from below they pile fresh ones on top, and they can pole a whole island to a new spot (cultural creation born on the lake; dinner-test payoff). T3: their islands, their reed houses, and even their curved boats with animal-head prows are all built from the SAME totora reed of the lake. T3: it is the largest lake in South America by volume, an endorheic Altiplano lake that drains only to smaller Lake Poopo. T4: underwater archaeologists have raised ancient Tiwanaku offerings and stonework from the lakebed; the lake was SACRED to the Inca, who held that the creator Viracocha and the first Inca rose from its waters (Inca belief -- flag it). T4: the Isla del Sol ('Island of the Sun') holds Inca ruins and, by legend, the birthplace of the sun. T5: at this altitude the air carries roughly a third less oxygen, and the huge lake acts as a HEAT BUFFER, moderating the frigid Altiplano so people can farm potatoes and herd where it would otherwise be too cold.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Titicaca, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Titicaca, Atlas Obscura 'Uros', geographypin.com. Figures: 3,812 m elevation, 8,372 km2, largest South American lake by volume, totora-reed Uros islands, drains to Lake Poopo.
framing_note: The Uros and Inca are FULL cultures, told with wonder and zero condescension (moral_vision sec 4 -- no 'primitive'/'exotic'), hence vision_mandated. Distractors = other high/large lakes (Poopo, Salar de Uyuni, Lake Tahoe, the Caspian). Accuracy rail: label the Viracocha/first-Inca origin as INCA BELIEF, not fact; 'highest navigable' is the standard careful claim (higher lakes exist that boats do not ply). Dinner-test = the movable floating reed islands. LANE: the totora reed island is a CULTURAL creation born on the lake (geography), not a craft-recipe.

name: Lake Superior and the Great Lakes
scope: The largest of the five North American Great Lakes, on the US-Canada border. T1: Superior is the LARGEST freshwater lake on Earth by surface area (82,100 km2) -- big enough to hold every other Great Lake plus three more Lake Eries (size is the hook; answer = 'largest freshwater lake by area'). T2: together the five Great Lakes hold about ONE-FIFTH (~21%) of all the surface fresh water on the planet. T3: Superior is so deep and cold (averaging ~4 C) that, sailors say, 'it never gives up its dead' -- the frigid water keeps drowned bodies from rising, a real cold-water place-fact. T3: fierce autumn storms -- the 'Gales of November' -- brew waves that sink ships along its coast (the wreck coast). T4: the whole lake system was gouged out by ICE-AGE glaciers grinding south, then filled with meltwater ~10,000 years ago (teach 'glacial scouring'). T5: freed of the mile-thick ice that once pressed it down, the land is still slowly REBOUNDING upward (isostatic rebound), tilting the water gently southward. Further rung: Superior's north shore and Isle Royale sit on 1.1-billion-year basalt of the Midcontinent Rift, where North America once began to tear apart.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Superior, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Superior, USGS Great Lakes, NOAA. Figures: 82,100 km2 (largest freshwater lake by area), Great Lakes ~21% of surface fresh water, avg ~4 C, glacial origin, Midcontinent Rift basalt.
framing_note: Distractors = other freshwater superlatives (Baikal = most water/deepest, Tanganyika = longest, Victoria = largest tropical). Accuracy rail: Superior is largest by AREA while Baikal is larger by VOLUME -- keep the two superlatives distinct so both stay live. Teach 'glacial scouring' and 'isostatic rebound'. Dinner-test = the cold deep that 'never gives up its dead' / the Gales of November. LANE: keep answers to the lake and its earth-history, not shipping economics.
history_overlap: The Edmund Fitzgerald wreck could brush a maritime-history episode -- keep the storm rung on Superior's cold-and-gale place-fact, not the ship's crew story.

name: Lake Tanganyika
scope: A long, deep rift lake in East Africa shared by Tanzania, the DR Congo, Burundi, and Zambia. T2: Tanganyika is the world's LONGEST freshwater lake -- 673 km, a thin blue ribbon threaded down the Great Rift Valley (its shape is the hook; answer = 'longest lake'). T3: its floor drops 1,470 m, making it the world's SECOND-deepest lake, after Baikal. T3: it holds about 16% of the world's available fresh water -- a single African lake with a sixth of the planet's liquid fresh water. T4: like Baikal it fills a RIFT where the continent is slowly tearing apart along the East African Rift -- a lake in a crack in a splitting Africa (teach 'rift lake'; it may one day widen into an ocean). T5: below roughly 100 m its deep water holds NO oxygen and has not mixed for thousands of years -- life crowds the thin sunlit top, a still, lightless 'dead' deep beneath (place-fact; dinner-test payoff). Further rung: on its shore at Ujiji in 1871, Henry Morton Stanley found the lost explorer David Livingstone ('Dr. Livingstone, I presume?').
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Tanganyika, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Tanganyika, Britannica 'Lake Tanganyika', African Great Lakes Inform. Figures: 673 km long (longest), 1,470 m deep (2nd deepest), ~16% of world fresh water, East African Rift, anoxic below ~100 m.
framing_note: Distractors = other deep/long/ancient lakes (Baikal deepest, Malawi, Superior, Victoria). Teach 'rift lake' and the stratified anoxic deep. Dinner-test = the lightless, oxygen-less deep / a sixth of Earth's fresh water in one lake. LANE: Tanganyika's famous cichlid fish are an ANIMAL-bank story -- keep the answer the PLACE-fact (the oxygen-less deep, the rift), never the fish's evolution or anatomy.
history_overlap: The Stanley-meets-Livingstone-at-Ujiji rung brushes an exploration-history episode -- keep it a place-anchored 'on this shore' fact, or drop it, if history covers it.

name: Crater Lake
scope: A deep blue lake filling a volcanic caldera in Oregon's Cascade Range. T1: Crater Lake fills the bowl left when a whole MOUNTAIN -- Mount Mazama -- blew its top and collapsed about 7,700 years ago; the giant pit it left is called a CALDERA (scene sets it up; teach and answer = 'a caldera'). T2: no river flows in or out -- the lake is filled ONLY by rain and snowmelt, which is why its water is so pure and vividly DEEP BLUE. T3: at 594 m (1,949 ft) it is the DEEPEST lake in the United States. T3: the water is so clear that sunlight sinks deep and scatters back intense blue -- a white dinner plate stays visible ~30 m down. T4: a small cinder cone pokes above the surface -- WIZARD ISLAND -- a baby volcano that grew inside the caldera after the collapse (named wonder). T4: a full-size hemlock log, the 'OLD MAN OF THE LAKE', has floated UPRIGHT and bobbing around the lake since at least 1896, preserved by the cold pure water (dinner-test payoff). T5: Mazama's eruption was roughly 40 times bigger than Mount St. Helens in 1980; its ASH blanketed the Northwest and is still a dated marker layer geologists dig up. Further rung: the Klamath people witnessed the eruption, and their oral tradition tells of a battle between the sky spirit Skell and Llao of the underworld (oral tradition -- flag it).
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Crater_Lake, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Man_of_the_Lake, nps.gov/crla, USGS 'Geology of Crater Lake', volcano.oregonstate.edu. Figures: Mazama collapse ~7,700 yr BP, 594 m depth (deepest in US, 7th deepest worldwide), Wizard Island cinder cone, Old Man floating since 1896.
framing_note: Distractors = other deep/blue/volcanic lakes (Lake Tahoe, a Yellowstone caldera lake, Lake Toba, Kelimutu). Teach 'caldera' before testing it. Accuracy rail: Mazama collapsed ~7,700 yr ago; Crater is deepest IN THE US (Baikal, Tanganyika and others are deeper worldwide) -- keep the 'in the US' qualifier so the superlative is true; the Klamath eruption-battle is ORAL TRADITION -- label it. Dinner-test = the Old Man of the Lake standing upright for 130 years.

name: Lake Natron
scope: A shallow, blood-red soda lake in the East African Rift of northern Tanzania. T2: Natron glows deep RED and orange even from space -- the color comes from salt-loving MICROBES (cyanobacteria) that thrive in its scalding, caustic water (the red is the hook; answer = 'living microbes/algae', not a mineral; teach 'soda lake'). T3: the water is a natural LYE -- loaded with sodium carbonate (natron, the very salt the Egyptians used to mummify), with a pH near 10.5 and temperatures up to ~60 C. T4: animals that die in or near it get COATED and preserved in the hard soda crust, looking eerily 'turned to stone' -- but the truth is it does NOT petrify the living instantly; it slowly encrusts the dead (accuracy rail; dinner-test payoff told honestly). T4: deadly as it is, Natron is the single most important BREEDING ground on Earth for the lesser flamingo -- the caustic water and soda islands keep predators away from the nests (place-fact: the water PROTECTS the colony). T5: Natron sits below OL DOINYO LENGAI, the only volcano on Earth that erupts cold, black CARBONATITE lava, which weathers to white powder and feeds the lake its strange soda chemistry (teach 'carbonatite'; the source of the soda).
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Natron, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Natron, Africa Check 'Lake Natron not deadliest... bodies calcified not turned to stone', Live Science, Smithsonian. Figures: pH ~10.5 (up to ~12 seasonally), up to ~60 C, sodium-carbonate crust, lesser-flamingo breeding site, fed by Ol Doinyo Lengai carbonatite.
framing_note: The accuracy rail is load-bearing: the 'turns animals to stone' story is SENSATIONALIZED -- the soda slowly encrusts animals that ALREADY DIED; never claim it petrifies the living. Distractors = other colored/salt lakes (Lake Retba pink, the Grand Prismatic Spring, the Dead Sea, Lake Magadi). Teach 'soda lake' and 'carbonatite'. Dinner-test = the soda-encrusted 'statue' animals, told truthfully. LANE: the lesser flamingo is an ANIMAL -- the geography answer is that the caustic water and soda islands PROTECT the nesting colony (a place-fact), never the bird's biology.

name: The Pink Lakes -- Hillier and Retba
scope: Two famously bubblegum-pink saltwater lakes -- Lake Hillier on Middle Island, Western Australia, and Lac Rose (Lake Retba) in Senegal. T2: Lake Hillier is a permanent BUBBLEGUM-PINK -- and it stays pink even when you scoop the water into a glass, so the color is life in the water, not a trick of the sky (the pink is the hook; answer = 'living microbes/algae'). T3: the color comes from Dunaliella salina algae (plus pink salt-loving haloarchaea) that pump out a red-orange pigment, BETA-CAROTENE -- the same pigment that colors carrots -- when stressed by extreme salt (teach the pigment). T4: at Senegal's Lake Retba, salt is up to ten times the ocean's, and workers wade in to hand-harvest SALT from the rosy brine, greasing their skin with shea butter against the sting (place-work). Dinner-test payoff: it stays pink in the glass because the color is living microbes.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Hillier, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Hillier, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_lake, and the 2022 cross-kingdom metagenomic study (NCBI PMC9768965) identifying Dunaliella, Salinibacter, Halobacillus, Psychroflexus, Halorubrum. Hillier salinity ~28%.
framing_note: Distractors = other colored/salt lakes (Lake Natron red, the Dead Sea, the Grand Prismatic hot spring, Laguna Colorada). Accuracy rail: the color is a MICROBIAL pigment (Dunaliella salina + haloarchaea, beta-carotene), NOT a sky reflection and NOT a single 'mineral' -- recent metagenomics shows it is a whole microbe community. Dinner-test = it stays pink in the glass. LANE: Retba's salt harvesting is place-work (a mineral), not a cooking/food-origin ladder.

name: Lake Nyos
scope: A small, deep crater lake in the volcanic highlands of northwestern Cameroon. T3: on one night in 1986 the quiet little lake silently killed 1,746 people and thousands of cattle in the valleys below -- with no flood, no wave, and no fire (the mystery death is the hook; answer = 'a cloud of carbon dioxide'). T4: the killer was CARBON DIOXIDE -- volcanic CO2 had built up under pressure in the lake's deep water for decades until a disturbance let it burst out like a shaken soda bottle; the heavy, invisible gas rolled downhill and smothered every breathing thing -- a 'LIMNIC ERUPTION' (teach the term; earth-process). T5: only THREE lakes on Earth are known to do this -- Nyos and Monoun in Cameroon and giant Lake Kivu on the Rwanda-Congo border -- so engineers now run DEGASSING PIPES that fountain the deep gas out slowly and safely (the fix). Dinner-test payoff: an invisible lake that put a whole valley to sleep overnight.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Nyos_disaster, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Nyos_disaster, Britannica 'Lake Nyos disaster', ScienceAlert. Figures: 21 Aug 1986, 1,746 deaths + ~3,500 livestock, 100,000-300,000 t CO2, degassing tubes installed, three known limnic-eruption lakes (Nyos, Monoun, Kivu).
framing_note: A grim but true earth-science gem -- tell it SOBERLY, not gorily; the payoff is the STRANGE MECHANISM (a lake as a shaken soda bottle), not the body count. Distractors = other lake hazards (a tsunami, a caldera collapse, Lake Kivu, Dominica's Boiling Lake). Accuracy rail: ~1,746 deaths, 21 Aug 1986, CO2 (not a poison-gas attack); the exact trigger is uncertain (landslide / cold-rain mixing) -- say 'a disturbance'. Teach 'limnic eruption'. Dinner-test = the valley that fell asleep and never woke.

name: Salar de Uyuni
scope: The world's largest salt flat -- a blinding-white plain in the Bolivian Altiplano, the ghost of a vanished inland sea. T2: Uyuni is the world's LARGEST salt flat -- 10,582 km2, about the size of Jamaica -- a dead-flat white plain of salt where a giant lake once stood (the white expanse is the hook; answer = 'a salt flat / dried lake'). T3: it is the dried-up floor of a prehistoric inland sea (Lake Minchin/Tauca) that evaporated more than 10,000 years ago, leaving a salt crust up to ~10 m thick. T3: in the dry season the salt hardens into a tessellated pattern of POLYGON tiles stretching to the horizon. T4: when a thin sheet of rain covers it, the flat becomes the world's largest MIRROR -- sky and clouds reflect so perfectly that walkers seem to float in the air (dinner-test payoff). T4: it is so PERFECTLY flat -- varying under a metre over 100+ km -- that satellites use it to calibrate their instruments from orbit. T5: beneath the crust lies a brine holding perhaps a QUARTER of the world's known lithium, the metal in phone and car batteries -- making a dead lake one of the most coveted places on Earth (keep it geology, not trade policy).
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Salar_de_Uyuni, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salar_de_Uyuni, Discovery 'world's largest natural mirror', geologyscience.com. Figures: 10,582 km2, 3,656 m elevation, ~8-10 m salt crust, dried from Pleistocene Lake Minchin/Tauca, flatness <1 m over the whole area, ~22% of world lithium resources in the brine.
framing_note: An inland SEA that died -- fits the salt/endorheic theme. Distractors = other salt flats / dried lakes (Bonneville Salt Flats, the Aral/Aralkum, Salinas Grandes, Etosha Pan). Accuracy rail: it is a dried Pleistocene lake (Minchin/Tauca), and the mirror needs a thin rain sheet (seasonal, Nov-Mar). Dinner-test = the world's largest mirror. LANE: keep the lithium rung about the GEOLOGY (brine under a dead lake), not the battery supply chain (that dates the bank and drifts into economics).

name: Lake Victoria
scope: Africa's largest lake, a shallow tropical inland sea shared by Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya. T2: Victoria is the LARGEST lake in Africa and the largest TROPICAL lake on Earth -- a freshwater sea nearly the size of Ireland (~59,900 km2) (size is the hook; answer = 'largest tropical lake / largest in Africa'). T3: it is the chief source of the NILE -- the White Nile begins where the lake spills north at Jinja, Uganda, launching the world's longest river on its ~6,600 km journey to Egypt (place-fact; dinner-test payoff). T3: unlike deep Baikal or Tanganyika, Victoria is SHALLOW -- only ~40 m deep on average -- and geologically YOUNG, having dried out completely and refilled within roughly the last 15,000 years. T4: it was not carved by a rift; instead the land around it slowly WARPED and tilted, ponding rivers backward into a broad, shallow basin (earth-process; the down-warp, contrasted with rift lakes). T5: warm water plus equatorial heat brews violent afternoon THUNDERSTORMS almost daily, making Victoria one of the most lightning-struck and dangerous-for-fishermen lakes on Earth.
source: Grokipedia (grokipedia.com/page/Lake_Victoria, attempted -- 403); corroborated via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria, Britannica 'Lake Victoria', NASA Earth Observatory. Figures: ~59,947 km2 (largest in Africa, largest tropical, 2nd-largest freshwater lake by area after Superior), avg depth ~40 m, White Nile outflow at Jinja, formed by continental down-warping ~15 kyr ago.
framing_note: Distractors = other great lakes / Nile facts (Tanganyika, Lake Albert, Lake Malawi, the Blue Nile's source at Lake Tana). Accuracy rail: local peoples long knew the Nile's source; John Speke (1858) was the first EUROPEAN to report it -- do NOT call it 'discovered'. Victoria is the largest tropical lake / largest in Africa but SECOND-largest freshwater lake by area after Superior -- keep the qualifier so it stays true. Dinner-test = the birthplace of the Nile. LANE: the Nile's course through Egypt is HISTORY's -- keep this rung on the SOURCE/outflow at Jinja; the Nile perch that wiped out Victoria's cichlids is an ANIMAL story -- do not build it here.
history_overlap: History/Egyptian-geography ladders own the Nile in Egypt -- keep Victoria's rung to the SOURCE/outflow at Jinja, not the river's Egyptian course.
